hairline.note: One step lighter than the first build (#2a2d33) so hairlines survive a projector.

input-edge.note: Lifted from #353840 with the hairline. Hover border, outline buttons, switch-off track.

headline.purpose: Settings and Privacy page title (22px); onboarding step titles use it at 24px.

title.purpose: Current breadcrumb segment, chat heading, sidebar wordmark.

body-answer.purpose: Assistant answers in the chat; carries the marks.

body.purpose: Chat intro, user messages, descriptions, tree rows.

file-name.purpose: File names in rows; scan status title.

small.purpose: Source chips, the 'Possibly related files' label, the welcome screen's sample source (13px).

label.purpose: Column headers, section labels, counts, scan meta, tour step count; tabular figures.

citation.purpose: Citation numeral in a small yellow-outlined tab (12px, ~1.1rem tall, outline yellow at 55%); fills yellow with ink-on text on hover.

shadows.name: floating-menu
shadows.purpose: Dropdown menus only (inherited from the component library); dialogs use the ring alone. Nothing on the ground has a shadow.

shadows.name: tour-card
shadows.purpose: The tour card only: floating ring plus a deeper shadow over the dimmed window.

shadows.name: tour-scrim
shadows.value: 0 0 0 9999px rgb(10 11 13 / 0.62); outline: 1px solid color-mix(in oklab, #e8e5dd 22%, transparent)
shadows.purpose: Tour spotlight cut-out: dims everything but the explained part of Home. Not a lift.

focus.name: focus-ring-button
focus.purpose: Buttons (ring token = yellow at 70%, applied at 50%).

focus.name: selection
focus.purpose: Text selection, distinct from any mark.

focus.name: scrollbar
focus.value: scrollbar-width: thin; scrollbar-color: #34373e transparent; webkit: 10px, thumb #34373e with 3px ground border, radius 999px

motion.name: mark-in
motion.purpose: Highlighter swipe wipe-in (background-size 0% to 100%). None under reduced motion.

motion.name: row-hover
motion.purpose: File row background and actions-button opacity. None under reduced motion.

motion.name: menu-in
motion.purpose: Dropdown menu and dialog entry (component library).

motion.name: tour-glide
motion.purpose: Tour spotlight and card moving between steps; the one authored motion besides the wipe. None under reduced motion.

motion.name: switch-thumb
motion.purpose: Switch thumb slide and track colour. None under reduced motion.

motion.name: quick-mark
motion.purpose: Mark on the active quick-search row; shortened because the selection follows the arrow keys.

breakpoints.name: file-list-narrow
breakpoints.purpose: Name column gets a 9rem floor (1.4fr vs 1fr), gaps 10px.

breakpoints.name: window-min
breakpoints.purpose: Minimum app window; side columns flex with clamp().

breakpoints.name: short
breakpoints.purpose: Custom variant `short:` for the 900x600 minimum window; tightens onboarding vertical spacing so the primary action stays above the fold.

layout.sidebarFooter: hairline, scan status, hairline, then Settings and Privacy links side by side (muted, md corners, Muted fill on hover)
layout.pageRow: hairline-ruled, 14px vertical padding, title/description left, controls right

extensions.coverage: Coverage: this system was set by the Home window (sidebar, file list, chat) and then extended, on the same grammar, to Onboarding, the Settings and Privacy pages, the first-time tour, the first-close dialog and the quick-search widget. Onboarding no longer uses card containers or a yellow-filled step indicator. There is no light theme; every value here is the dark theme.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Highlighter Yellow action, used for Send once there is text to send.

narrative.overview:
The folder reads like pages the user has already marked up. Everything sits on a matte graphite ground in warm paper-white type, separated by hairline rules rather than cards or shadows. Colour is almost absent until something matters: the open folder, the selected file, a cited fact in a chat answer, a finished scan. Then a flat highlighter swipe is drawn behind the words, the way a student marks a printout.

Density is that of a calm file manager: one file per line, a margin index on the left, a reading column for answers on the right. The interface frames the user's files and stays out of the way; motion is limited to short state changes, the one wipe of the highlighter, and the first-time tour's spotlight gliding on the same curve. The system deliberately refuses the category default of grey cards with one glowing accent: inks are flat, never glows, and each ink has exactly one job.
keyCharacteristics: Matte graphite ground, warm paper-white text, hairline rules for structure.
Four flat highlighter inks, each bound to a single meaning.
The highlighter swipe (`.mark`) is the signature: drawn shape, slanted ragged ends, wiped in left to right.
One-line ruled file rows; no file cards.
Geist throughout, tabular figures for every count.
Flat: no shadows on the ground; depth only for floating menus and dialogs.

rules.name: The One Job Rule
rules.body: Each ink means one thing everywhere: yellow = selected / cited, green = done, pink = removed / failed, blue = in progress. Never use an ink for decoration, branding a section, or a meaning outside its job.

rules.name: The Earned Ink Rule
rules.body: Ink appears only where something matters right now. At rest a screen is graphite and paper; if a viewport shows more than a handful of marks, something is marked that should not be.

rules.name: The No Dimmed Ink Rule
rules.body: A control that is unavailable falls back to plain graphite, never to a faded ink. The empty Send button is secondary graphite with muted text, and turns yellow only when there is something to send.

rules.name: The Selection Is Not A Mark Rule
rules.body: Text selection is blue-tinted graphite (`ink-blue` at 38%) with paper-white text, so the user's own selection can never be mistaken for a highlighter mark.

rules.name: The Tabular Count Rule
rules.body: Every number that counts or measures (file totals, folder counts, indexed / unreadable counts, citation numerals, ETA) uses tabular figures.

rules.name: The Weight Not Size Rule
rules.body: Distinguish levels with weight (400 / 500 / 600) and paper vs. muted colour. No size above 15px appears inside the Home window.

rules.name: The Hairline Not Shadow Rule
rules.body: Separate things with a 1px Hairline rule. A shadow is reserved for something floating above the window; nothing that sits in the page gets one.

dos: Do use the highlighter mark for exactly three kinds of thing: the current selection (open folder, selected file, open Settings / Privacy page, current onboarding step, active quick-search row), a cited fact, and a completed scan.
Do keep every ink to its one job: yellow selected / cited, green done, pink removed / failed, blue in progress.
Do separate content with 1px Hairline rules and the graphite surface steps.
Do list files as one-line ruled rows (icon · name · description · ⋯) and let the name column win when space is narrow.
Do set every count and citation numeral in tabular figures.
Do let side columns flex with `clamp()` (sidebar 13.5–17.5rem, chat 18–25rem) so the window works down to 900×600.
Do make the swipe static and drop row transitions under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
Do fall back to plain graphite for unavailable controls instead of a faded ink.
Do set the chosen option of a segmented control in raised graphite, and reserve yellow for a switch that is on.
Do colour every progress bar blue (`--progress-ink: var(--ink-blue)`); a bar is "in progress".
Do say in a confirm dialog exactly what goes and what stays before the pink button.
donts: Don't put files or panels in cards, or give anything on the ground a shadow; shadows belong only to floating layers (menus, the tour card).
Don't render an ink as a glow, gradient or blurred halo; marks are flat swipes behind text.
Don't use yellow for "done" or green for "selected"; that breaks the one-job inks.
Don't mark more than the cited claim; long claims get only their last sentence marked.
Don't swipe the same selection twice (the tree brightens the selected file, the list marks it).
Don't style text selection like a highlighter mark.
Don't ink matched search words; brighten them. The mark belongs to the selected row.
Don't add motion beyond state changes, the wipe and the tour's glide.
